reading.body:
CyrusOne Cincinnati (CIN2) publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, making it the third-largest of only eight Ohio data centers with disclosed power figures and 18 percent of the state's disclosed IT load.

At 40 kW per rack, 11 MW supports roughly 275 racks. At 320 kW per GPU cluster, it could host about 34 clusters. That is below the scale required for frontier model training, which typically demands 100+ MW campuses now under construction in power-rich jurisdictions.

The facility's PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II certifications point to regulated financial, healthcare, and federal workloads rather than unconstrained AI research. Ohio has 77 mapped data centers, but only eight publish power figures, so the ranking reflects disclosed capacity only. The data does not show whether AI workloads actually run at CIN2, and no announced expansion is recorded.
